question:
A 60-year-old woman presents with a one-month history of worsening dyspnea, a nonproductive
cough, and weight loss. She now experiences dyspnea at rest and severe shortness of breath when
climbing one flight of stairs. She denies chest pain, orthopnea, or paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea. Her
medical history includes nonischemic cardiomyopathy and sustained ventricular tachycardia, for which

she has an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator. She was started on oral amiodarone several months
ago for recurrent ventricular tachycardia. Her current medications include lisinopril, carvedilol, and
torsemide. On examination, the patient is afebrile, with a heart rate of 64 beats per minute and blood
pressure of 129/65 mm Hg. Jugular venous pressure is normal, and there is no lower-extremity edema.
Cardiovascular examination is unremarkable, but pulmonary examination reveals bilateral inspiratory
crackles. An electrocardiogram shows normal sinus rhythm, and a chest radiograph demonstrates
bilateral, diffuse interstitial opacities. What is the most appropriate management strategy for this
patient? Answer Choices: (A) Switch amiodarone to dofetilide without additional treatment (B) Continue
amiodarone and add oral prednisone (C) Perform a bronchoscopy and continue amiodarone until
confirmed diagnosis (D) Stop amiodarone and start oral prednisone plus another antiarrhythmic agent
(E) Stop amiodarone and give no additional treatment (F) Initiate diuretic therapy to manage suspected
pulmonary edema (G) Start high-dose intravenous methylprednisolone without stopping amiodarone
(H) Discontinue all medications and initiate mechanical ventilation (I) Stop amiodarone and initiate
bronchodilator therapy with albuterol (J) Stop amiodarone and start high-dose intravenous
methylprednisolone plus another antiarrhythmic agent
 A. Stop amiodarone and start high-dose intravenous methylprednisolone plus another
antiarrhythmic agent
B. Switch amiodarone to dofetilide without additional treatment
C. Continue amiodarone and add oral prednisone
D. Perform a bronchoscopy and continue amiodarone until confirmed diagnosis
E. Stop amiodarone and give no additional treatment
F. Stop amiodarone and start oral prednisone plus another antiarrhythmic agent
G. Initiate diuretic therapy to manage suspected pulmonary edema
H. Discontinue all medications and initiate mechanical ventilation
I. Start high-dose intravenous methylprednisolone without stopping amiodarone
J. Stop amiodarone and initiate bronchodilator therapy with albuterol
